title: Deal Terms release package 1.2.0
description: Package contract 1.2.0. The release manifest of a Deal Terms package. The per-deal document is $defs/dealDocument and the in-package corpus manifest is $defs/corpusManifest; a validator points at those directly for deals/<deal_key>/deal.json and corpus/corpus-manifest.json. This schema constrains shape and vocabulary only. It cannot check a content ID or a SHA-256: that is verify.mjs, and a package is not valid until verify.mjs exits 0 on it. Every ID in this schema is contentId(domain, record) or sha256Hex(bytes) as defined in the producer's lib/canonical-v2/canonical-bytes.js.

package_schema_version.description: Semantic version of the package contract. 1.0.0 was draft 1; 1.1.0 added transaction_id and the typed field quartet; 1.2.0 adds fact_state, source units, limitations, release lineage and the transaction-shaped corpus.

production_release_id.description: The producer's identifier for this release. Immutable; a re-cut is a new release.

supersedes_release_manifest_id.description: The release_manifest_id of this corpus's previous release, or null for the first. Null if and only if release_sequence is 1. A release never supersedes itself.

release_sequence.description: Strictly increasing per corpus_id. Each package is a COMPLETE snapshot of its corpus: an occurrence present in a predecessor and absent from a successor has been withdrawn, never merely omitted. A consumer activates exactly one verified release per corpus at a time and rolls back by activating the exact predecessor id. released_at is informational and must not be used to order releases.

producer_commit.description: The producer's git commit the package was cut from. Not a path, not a branch name.

public.description: True if and only if release_state is PUBLIC. verify.mjs enforces the biconditional.

released_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant, second precision. An input to release_manifest_id, so it is fixed at cut time.

deals.description: Ordered by deal_key. One entry per deal document in the package.

files.description: Every file in the package except manifest.json itself, ordered by path. The set must equal the files on disk exactly: no extras, no omissions.

hex64.description: A 64-character lowercase hexadecimal digest: either sha256Hex(bytes) or contentId(domain, record) from lib/canonical-v2/canonical-bytes.js.

cik.description: SEC Central Index Key, zero-padded to ten digits (the SEC_CIK convention in lib/canonical-v2/entity-subject.js).

accession.description: SEC accession number, NNNNNNNNNN-NN-NNNNNN (the ACCESSION_RE of lib/canonical-v2/deal-source-binding.js).

roleKey.description: A document role key from the producer's document role registry (ROLE_KEY_RE of lib/canonical-v2/deal-source-binding.js).

reasonCode.description: An upper-snake reason code. The vocabulary is open at v1; the codes known when v1 was written are listed in the prose contract.

transactionId.description: The consumer-minted transaction-level deal ID (Q-0001 section 2's deal_id, over a PUBLIC_MA_DEAL/V1 payload of target CIK, transaction anchor and ordinal). A package NEVER mints one: it arrives through the corpus manifest and is copied into the deal document unchanged. Null where the consumer has not keyed the deal, and a package containing any null transaction_id can never carry release_state PUBLIC.

dealIdentity.description: The four fields whose content ID is the deal_key: contentId('DEAL_TERMS_DEAL_KEY/V1', this object).

agreement_id.description: The producer's canonical-text content ID for the agreement.

retrieval_url_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the retrieval URL. The URL itself is not carried; a consumer reconstructs the EDGAR location from issuer_cik and accession.

sec_document_name.description: The SEC document name from the admitted-source receipt, so a consumer can open the exact admitted document (Q-0002 section 2). A filing-side name, never a producer path: no separator is permitted. Null where the receipt did not record it, and a package containing any null cannot be PUBLIC.

sec_document_sequence.description: The document's sequence within the filing. Null under the same conditions as sec_document_name, with the same PUBLIC consequence.

provenance.description: Document identity by content, never by location. No repository path appears here or anywhere else in a package.

factState.description: The semantic state of one field, independent of its claim's review state (Q-0002 section 1, A-0006 ruling 1). PRESENT: a value was found; zero and false are PRESENT. ABSENT: the source unit named in examined_source_unit_id was read and does not state it. NOT_APPLICABLE: the field does not apply, with a governed reason_code. NOT_EXAMINED: the occurrence's subtype profile does not carry the field. FAILED: extraction could not resolve it, which is legal only under a REVIEW_ONLY claim carrying issue codes. ABSENT, NOT_APPLICABLE and NOT_EXAMINED are three different things and a consumer must not collapse them, nor render any of them as zero, false or empty.

source_unit_id.description: The source unit this evidence sits in. Must exist in the deal's source unit set.

evidenceSpan.description: Half-open [start_byte, end_byte) in UTF-8 bytes over the canonical text, with the quoted text bound to both its width and its SHA-256.

code.description: From the producer's governed limitation vocabulary.

text.description: The limitation text as it appears in the ruling record. A consumer displays this beside the answer; it must not paraphrase it.

ruling_id.description: Content ID of the ruling record the limitation comes from.

limitation.description: Required on every APPROVED_LIMITED claim and forbidden on every other (A-0006 ruling 3). An APPROVED_LIMITED answer displayed without its limitation is a misrepresentation, so the verifier refuses a package that omits it.

kind.description: The provenance kind of this context, from the re-plan's source-closure rule: the parent chain up to SECTION, the governing chapeau, and the Article chapeau for representations.

node_occurrence_id.description: M2 node occurrence identity. Claims and evidence spans reference a unit by this.

document_order.description: Position in the document. Unique within the set, and the set is ordered by it.

text.description: The FULL canonical text of the authored unit, so a consumer never has to reconstruct a provision from excerpts (Q-0002 section 2). Whole-agreement text is not carried; its SHA-256 and byte length are, in provenance.

valueType.description: FACT_VALUE_TYPES of lib/canonical-v2/m7-v2-contract.js (line 434 at the time of writing).

evidence_spans.description: Non-empty if and only if fact_state is PRESENT.

examined_source_unit_id.description: Non-null if and only if fact_state is ABSENT: the unit that was read and does not state the field. It is what makes an absence a finding rather than a silence.

reason_code.description: Non-null if and only if fact_state is NOT_APPLICABLE.

typed_value.description: The machine-readable value, or null in every fact_state except PRESENT. Its shape is fixed by value_type, exactly as lib/canonical-v2/m7-v2-contract.js validates an atomic fact: PARTY_SET is {parties:[string,...]}, non-empty and unique; PARTY, ENUM, DEFINED_TERM, DATE and REFERENCE are non-empty strings; BOOLEAN is a boolean; NUMBER and PERCENTAGE are finite numbers; DURATION and PERIOD are {bound_type, count, unit} with unit in DAY/WEEK/MONTH/YEAR and bound_type in EXACT/WITHIN/AT_LEAST (DURATION) or EXACT/WITHIN (PERIOD); MONEY is {amount, currency}. JSON Schema cannot express the dependency, so verify.mjs enforces it.

unit.description: The currency for MONEY, the DAY/WEEK/MONTH/YEAR unit for DURATION and PERIOD, the literal PERCENT for PERCENTAGE, null otherwise. Derived from typed_value and checked by verify.mjs.

sort_value.description: A scalar derived deterministically from typed_value alone, so a consumer never parses a display string to sort. NUMBER and PERCENTAGE give the number; MONEY gives amount (sort within a unit, never across); BOOLEAN gives 0 or 1; DATE gives the ISO date string when it is YYYY-MM-DD, else null; DURATION and PERIOD give count multiplied by a sort-only day-equivalent (DAY 1, WEEK 7, MONTH 30, YEAR 365) which must never be used for date arithmetic; ENUM, PARTY, DEFINED_TERM and REFERENCE give the string; PARTY_SET gives null because a set has no scalar order. Null means this value type has no order, never that the value is unknown.

typed_value_digest.description: sha256Hex(canonicalJson(typed_value)), computed in every state including null, so it stays re-derivable. Two claims agree on a value exactly when these are equal.

sourceSpan.description: A half-open [start_byte, end_byte) span in UTF-8 bytes over the canonical text. verify.mjs requires end_byte > start_byte, utf8ByteLength(excerpt_text) === end_byte - start_byte, and sha256Hex(excerpt_text) === text_sha256.

claim_occurrence_id.description: M4 claim occurrence identity. Stable across revisions: a changed answer keeps this and gets a new claim_revision_id.

classification_levels.description: Index 0 is APPLIES_TO, index 1 is PROVISION_TYPE, then the profile's classification path.

state.description: The producer's three-part state. Only the combinations validStateCombination() permits are legal; verify.mjs enforces them.

classification_path.description: The claim's classification_levels values from index 1 onward, i.e. everything below APPLIES_TO.

summary_review_state.description: REVIEW_ONLY beats APPROVED_LIMITED beats NORMAL beats NO_COMPARISON, mirroring summariseOccurrenceStates(). NO_OUTPUT claims are never summarised.

source_unit_set_id.description: The source unit set at source_units/<deal_key>.json. Every source unit and evidence span a claim references must exist in it.

claims.description: Ordered by claim_occurrence_id, each occurrence appearing at most once.

corpusManifest.$comment: The schema for corpus/corpus-manifest.json. Every document in a released corpus is already admitted, so no field here is nullable except transaction_id. The pre-admission input records are corpus-manifest.schema.json.

corpus_id.description: The content ID of Ben's approved transaction-selection record (A-0006 ruling 5). It is CARRIED, never recomputed from the document keys in this package: deriving it here would let a package mint a corpus identity for a selection nobody approved.

selection_record_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the approved selection record's bytes, so the citation is checkable against the selection itself.

ben_approval_id.description: Content ID of Ben's approval of that selection.

transactions.description: Ordered by transaction_id with the unkeyed group, if any, last. Document admission records sit UNDER their transaction: one transaction may carry several documents (Q-0002 section 5). No deal_key appears under more than one transaction, and the documents across all transactions are exactly the deal documents in the package.

transaction_id.description: At most one transaction group may be unkeyed (null), holding documents the consumer has not yet keyed. A package containing one cannot be PUBLIC.
